value: Grown in far smaller amounts than Pinot Noir, though the region is well regarded for it.

value: Fresh and mineral, with a tight, fine bodied frame and citrus and white peach fruit.

value: A leading white grape here, standing out among the region's aromatic wines.
source_notes: nzwine: Riesling stands out among aromatics ; Wine Society: riesling listed as a key grape of Central Otago

value: Lighter and flintier than Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc, with a crisp, linear, stony finish.

value: The region's dominant grape, on which Gisborne built its name.
source_notes: nzwine: Chardonnay is the dominant variety ; Wine Companion: chardonnay is the dominant grape, almost half of plantings ; NZ Herald: made its name as New Zealand's chardonnay capital

value: One of the region's main white grapes, much of it grown in volume.
source_notes: Wine Companion: chardonnay followed by pinot gris and sauvignon blanc ; Wine Anorak: vineyards largely used for large volumes of Chardonnay, Pinot Gris and Sauvignon

value: One of the region's main white grapes, much of it grown in volume.
source_notes: Wine Companion: chardonnay followed by pinot gris and sauvignon blanc ; Wine Anorak: vineyards largely used for large volumes of Chardonnay, Pinot Gris and Sauvignon

value: Well structured, with dark fruit, spice and sometimes a hint of mint.
source_notes: nzwine: impressive structure, classic dark fruit and spice ; Wine Companion: cabernet dominant blends well structured with blackcurrant, spice and mint

value: A signature grape of the region and widely seen as its finest white.
source_notes: Wine Companion: Hawke's Bay arguably chardonnay's spiritual home ; Wine Anorak: which many rate as Hawke's Bay's star turn ; NZ Herald: renowned for its world class chardonnay

source_notes: nzwine: full bodied, lengthy, almost opulent with finely tuned acidity ; Wine Companion: fuller bodied, peach, melon and citrus, well judged acidity ; Wine Society: Hawke's Bay chardonnay full, powerful

value: The main partner of Cabernet Sauvignon in the region's signature Bordeaux style reds.
source_notes: Wine Companion: signature red is a Bordeaux style blend of merlot and cabernet sauvignon ; NZ Herald: Bordeaux red varieties like cabernets and merlot excel in hotter sites

source_notes: nzwine: drier years give fleshy, flavoursome wines ; Wine Companion: merlot dominant wines fresh and fragrant with firm, ripe tannins ; Wine Society: fragrant

value: Bold, ripe and spicy, with a rich and concentrated feel.
source_notes: nzwine: aromatic, spicy, bold ripe wines with good body ; Wine Companion: typically rich, powerful and concentrated

value: A minor red in this region, grown mostly on cooler, higher inland sites and a few coastal ones.
source_notes: nzwine: Pinot Noir from higher altitude river valley sites, cooler Central Hawke's Bay and coastal gravels ; Wine Companion: usually grown on elevated inland sites, region's flagship red is a Bordeaux blend

source_notes: nzwine: cherry, berry, plum to savoury earthy styles, soft and supple tannins ; Wine Companion: from fruit forward dark cherry and plum to more savoury examples

value: Widely planted, though Chardonnay and the red grapes carry more of the region's name.
source_notes: Wine Companion: one of the region's most planted varieties alongside chardonnay ; Wine Anorak: Sauvignon Blanc widely planted but Chardonnay is the star turn, reds from Gimblett Gravels famous

value: Riper and more tropical than in cooler regions, with a broader feel and softer acidity.

value: A leading red grape of the region, with the Gimblett Gravels its best known source.

value: A smaller but increasingly serious part of a region built on Sauvignon Blanc.

value: Crisp and well structured, with intense citrus and stone fruit.

value: Tighter and more structured than North Island Pinot Gris, with a pure and lively feel.

value: Grown mainly on the heavier clay soils and hillsides of the Southern Valleys.

value: Juicy and medium weight, with bright cherry and plum fruit and fine tannins.

value: Pure and lively, with citrus fruit, turning honeyed in late harvest styles.
source_notes: Wine Companion: aromatic, lemon and lime, late harvest styles show honey and floral notes ; nzwine: aromatics reflect the region's purity and vivacity (only the first half)

value: The region's defining grape, whose style made New Zealand wine known around the world.

value: Pungently aromatic and zesty, with vivid tropical fruit and a green, herbaceous streak.
source_notes: nzwine: pungently aromatic, vividly pure fruit, herbaceous and exotically tropical ; Wine Companion: zesty acidity, pungent aromatics, grassy, passionfruit ; NZ Herald: intensely aromatic, passionfruit and green herb driven

value: One of the region's leading grapes, with the best coming from the clay soils of the Moutere Hills.

value: One of the region's leading grapes, at its best on the clay hills of the Moutere.

value: Widely grown across both the Waimea Plains and the Moutere Hills.

value: More restrained than Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc, with good texture and a mineral edge.
source_notes: nzwine: a more elegant, restrained expression, lovely texture and minerality ; Firstleaf (retailer): softer and more subtle than Marlborough, gentle minerality

value: Increasingly treated as the region's leading white, beside Pinot Noir.
source_notes: NZ Herald: a move towards celebrating chardonnay as its key white ; nzwine: outstanding Pinot Noir, Chardonnay ; Wine Anorak: some of the most sought after Pinot Noir and Chardonnay in the country

value: The region's main grape, made by many small producers.

value: Ranges from light, perfumed and pretty to dark, concentrated and brooding.

value: Bright and vivid, made in every style from dry to sweet.

value: A smaller but well regarded part of the region's output, beside Pinot Noir.

value: Dense and richly flavoured, with plum fruit and a savoury undercurrent.

value: Made alongside Pinot Noir, especially around Martinborough.

value: The main white grape, grown beside Pinot Noir across the region.

value: The district's flagship grape, with a growing number of premium wines from single vineyards and old vines.
